A lion lay sleeping in the shade of a tree. A small mouse, hurrying home through the grass, ran straight across his nose. The lion woke with a roar and caught the mouse under one heavy paw. "Please," said the mouse, "let me go. I am small and I meant no harm. One day I may be able to help you." The lion laughed that such a tiny creature could ever help him, and he lifted his paw and let her run away. Not many days later, hunters came to the forest. They spread a strong rope net between the trees, and the lion walked into it. He pulled and twisted and roared, but the ropes only grew tighter. The mouse heard him. She came running and began to gnaw the ropes with her small sharp teeth. One strand, then another, then another. By morning the net fell open, and the lion walked free. "You laughed at me," said the mouse, "but now you know. A small friend is still a friend."
